topic: Jaw tension, stress and neck tightness

slides.headline: Clenching your jaw without noticing?
slides.sub: How jaw tension, stress and a tight neck often go together.

slides.title: They're closely linked
slides.body: The jaw, neck and upper shoulders share muscles and nerves, so tension in one often shows up in the others. Stress, long screen days and poor sleep can all add to it.

slides.title: Check your resting jaw
slides.body: Right now, are your teeth touching? At rest, lips gently closed, teeth apart, tongue resting on the roof of your mouth. Set a phone reminder to check in a few times a day.

slides.title: Loosen the neck and shoulders
slides.body: Every hour or so, roll your shoulders, gently tuck your chin and turn your head side to side. Short breaks from the screen often help more than one long stretch at night.

slides.title: Wind down before bed
slides.body: Slow breathing, a warm shower, or gentle circles with your fingertips on the muscle in front of your ear can help your jaw relax. Many people clench more during stressful weeks.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: See your dentist or GP if your jaw locks, clicks painfully or makes eating hard, or if you have new severe headaches, facial numbness, or pain after an injury.

slides.headline: Tight neck and jaw lately?
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess your neck, jaw and upper back, may use gentle hands-on care alongside exercise, and liaise with your dentist when needed. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Quick check: are your teeth touching right now?

The jaw, neck and upper shoulders are closely linked, so tension in one often shows up in the others. Stress, long screen days and poor sleep can all add to it.

At rest, your lips can be gently closed with teeth apart and tongue on the roof of your mouth. Try hourly shoulder rolls and gentle chin tucks, and wind down before bed with slow breathing or gentle jaw massage.

See your dentist or GP if your jaw locks, clicks painfully or makes eating hard, or if you have new severe headaches or facial numbness.
